definition: Yamaka — a figure of speech where the same word is used twice with different meaning. In Ghatakarpara v.21, the poet who conquers by yamakas is honored. The yamaka is the poem's self-referential device.

sources.claim: jīyeya yena kavinā yamakaiḥ pareṇa (may I be conquered by which poet, by yamakas, other)

translations.note: No English equivalent; 'repeated word figure' is descriptive.
